title: Run a decision meeting in 15 minutes
speaker: Comlogue exemplar · engineering leader
breakdown: Opens with the decision, the owner and the ask in nine words.
Each option gets the same two-beat shape, so they're easy to compare.
Names what would change the speaker's mind — which invites real disagreement.
Pauses separate ideas so the room can keep up and respond.

lines.text: Here's the decision. [pause] Here's who owns it. [pause] Disagree now, or commit.

lines.text: We have fifteen minutes, [pause] and one question: [pause] do we ship the new onboarding on Monday?

lines.text: Option one: ship Monday. [pause] We learn faster, [pause] and support is ready.

lines.text: Option two: wait two weeks. [pause] We fix the edge cases, [pause] and lose two weeks of data.
lines.display_text: Option two: wait two weeks. We fix the edge cases, and lose two weeks of data.

lines.text: My recommendation is to ship Monday, [pause] behind a flag, [pause] for ten percent of new users.

lines.text: Two reasons. [pause] The risky cases are rare. [pause] And the flag lets us roll back in minutes.

lines.text: What would change my mind? [pause] Evidence that the rare cases aren't rare.
